reason: The hypothesis relies on a specific dislocation-mechanism shift (screw-to-edge) induced by W, but the cited evidence only shows that Mo-containing alloys retain high-temperature strength (E1) and that a transition in slip mode occurs in MoNbTaVW (E3); no evidence is provided that W addition to TiVNbTa would cause this shift or that W itself promotes edge-dislocation dominance. The baseline TiVNbTa properties are stated but not directly supported by the cited passages.
premises: W addition dissolves into BCC matrix and increases lattice distortion
Increased lattice distortion promotes a shift from screw- to edge-dominated dislocation slip at high temperature
Edge-dislocation mechanism retains yield strength better at elevated temperatures
Mo-containing RHEAs (e.g., MoNbTaW, MoNbTaVW) show lower reduction in yield strength at high temperature
TiVNbTa baseline has low high-temperature strength (~330–423 MPa at 1273 K)
